steps.prompt: Add up $1 + 2 + 3 + \cdots + 100$ without adding one number at a time. Hint: pair the first number with the last.
steps.placeholder: Each pair makes… there are… pairs…

cards.title: Same step every time
cards.body: An arithmetic sequence adds the same number $d$ each time: $a, a + d, a + 2d, \ldots$ Term number $n$ is $a + (n - 1)d$: to reach term $n$ you take $n - 1$ steps. The number of terms from first to last is $\frac{\text{last} - \text{first}}{d} + 1$.

steps.text: From $7$ to $203$ is $196$, which is $\frac{196}{4} = 49$ steps.

try.prompt: How many steps of $4$ from $7$ to $203$?

cards.title: Sum = number of terms × average
cards.body: Pair the first and last, the second and second-last, …: each pair has the same total. So the sum is (number of terms) $\times$ $\frac{\text{first} + \text{last}}{2}$. The average of an arithmetic sequence is the average of its first and last terms, which is also its middle term.

try.prompt: What is the average of the terms?

steps.text: There are $50$ terms, so the sum is $50 \times 105 = 5250$.

cards.title: The common trap: fence posts
cards.body: The number of terms is the number of steps PLUS ONE. Term $n$ is $a + (n - 1)d$, not $a + nd$. And when you pair up terms, don't forget to divide by $2$.

prompts: Explain the fence-post rule to a friend with your own example.
